newsitem.title: USA: First Banks, First Commercial to join.
newsitem.headline: First Banks, First Commercial to join.

text.p: First Banks America Inc and First Commercial Bancorp Inc said Friday they have an agreement in principle to merge.
Under the deal, First Commercial shareholders would receive 0.8888 shares of First Banks common stock for each share of First Commercial stock they hold.
In total, First Commercial's shareholders would receive 752,038 shares of First Banks stock.
The deal is subject to the execution of a definitive agreement between the companies, approval by regulatory authorities and approval by shareholders of both banks.

Under the deal, First Commercial will be merged into a subsidiary of First Banks America. In addition, First Commercial's wholly owned subisidiary, First Commercial Bank, will be merged into First Banks' subsidiary, Sunrise Bank of California.
As of June 30, First Banks had total assets of $374 million and First Commercial had assets of $159 million, the companies said.
About 30 percent of First Banks' outstanding stock is publicly held, while the remaining 70 percent is owned by First Banks Inc, a St. Louis-based $3.8 billion bank holding company.
In addition, 61.5 percent of First Commercial is owned by First Banks Inc with the rest traded publicly.

"Maintaining a separate publicy held bank holding company for First Commercial Bank is a relatively expensive form of organization for a bank its size," First Commercial Chairman, President and Chief Executive Donald Williams said in a statement.
"The combination of the two companies not only eliminates this expense, but provides First Commercial Bancorp shareholders with a more liquid investment for their portfolios," he said.
In connection with the transaction, First Banks Inc has agreed to exchange $10 million of its note receivable from First Banks America for 804,000 shares of First Banks America common stock.
